newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Laura Ashley pleased with US Xmas.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Laura Ashley pleased with US Xmas.

text.p: Clothing and home decor retailer Laura Ashley Holdings Plc on Wednesday said it was pleased with Christmas trading, particularly in the United States.
Chief executive Ann Iverson said: "I thought we had a very good Christmas in the UK and as far as America goes, you can see we had a significant change in the business."
She told Reuters she was encouraged by the performance of new stores coming on line in the United States.

Like-for-like sales in North America were one percent ahead in the six weeks over Christmas and the New Year, but this was affected by the closure of 19 shops. The group said its new shops in the region were beginning to show top line growth.

Iverson, who earned a reputation for turning around retailers at Britain's Storehouse Plc, was hired in 1995 to try and boost Laura Ashley, which has struggled to overcome difficulties brought on by overexpansion in the 1980s.
In Britain, she said party frocks had done well over Christmas and that there had been a move away from the traditional Laura Ashley look of the 1980s.
Home furnishings also did well, especially accessories, gifts and bedlinens, she said.
Iverson said a recovery in the housing market had clearly helped demand for home decor products in the UK. "People are investing in their home, decorating in their home," she said.

Margins in Britain were up while in the United States they were flat or slightly ahead. In Europe, margins were down as were sales, which suffered from sluggish Christmas spending in Germany, France and the Benelux countries, she said.
The group's shares were two pence lower at 157 pence by 1204 GMT.
